title: Updating a unary tape vector
statement: Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $\rho : \{0,\ldots,R-1\} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a register assignment, let $t$ be a register, and let $m \in \mathbb{N}$. Replacing tape $t$ in the vector of unary tapes encoding $\rho$ by the unary tape encoding $m$ gives the vector of unary tapes encoding the assignment obtained by replacing $\rho(t)$ by $m$.
replaced:
For $v \in \mathbb{N}$ let $1^v$ be the unary tape whose cells $0, \dots, v-1$ hold $1$ and whose
other cells are blank. Let $\rho : \{0, \dots, R-1\} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $t$ be an index and
$m \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $\rho'$ agree with $\rho$ except that $\rho'(t) = m$. Then replacing
the $t$-th entry of the tape vector $(1^{\rho(r)})_r$ by $1^m$ gives the tape vector
$(1^{\rho'(r)})_r$.
